title: Mains study breakdown — Papers I and II
notice: Derived study guidance. Every unit below groups or subdivides official syllabus lines; it never adds a requirement of its own.

mains/paper-I.focus: Two halves that answer in the same three-hour paper: History and Geography. Treat them as one paper with two revision cycles rather than as two independent subjects.

mains/paper-I/part-a/unit-1.focus: A long chronological sweep. The danger is depth without sequence, so fix the timeline before adding detail.

units.title: Harappan to tenth century
units.note: The source sets the closing point at the tenth century, so stop there rather than carrying on into the Sultanate.

units.title: Eleventh to eighteenth century
units.note: Same four lenses as the earlier period — political, economic, social, cultural — so the two can be revised in parallel.

units.title: Sultanate and Mughal rule, and the rise of medieval culture
split: सल्तनत एवं मुगल शासक और उनका प्रशासन
units.note: Administration is named explicitly, so prepare revenue and administrative structure, not just rulers.

mains/paper-I/part-a/unit-2.focus: One dense line naming every major dynasty of Madhya Pradesh. The list is the syllabus, so nothing can be dropped.

units.title: Prehistoric and protohistoric Madhya Pradesh
units.note: Pair with the rock shelters and prehistoric sites already used for Prelims Paper I subject 2.

units.title: Dynasty-by-dynasty table
units.note: One row per dynasty — region, capital, notable ruler, coins or inscriptions, monuments. Eight groups here, and every one is examinable.

mains/paper-I/part-a/unit-3.focus: The colonial impact, the Indian response, and Madhya Pradesh's own freedom movement.

units.title: Economic and social impact of British rule
units.note: Keep land revenue, deindustrialisation and social change as three separate strands.

units.title: Indian response and the national movement
match: ब्रिटिश उपनिवेश के प्रति भारतीयों की प्रतिक्रिया
split: राष्ट्रीय स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन एवं इसके नेतृत्वकर्ता
units.note: The peasant and tribal revolts are listed before 1857, so treat them as a distinct strand, not as a footnote to it.

units.title: Freedom movement in Madhya Pradesh
units.note: State-level events and personalities; carries forward into Unit V.

mains/paper-I/part-a/unit-4.focus: Post-independence India, cultural heritage with a state focus, and heritage tourism.

units.title: Republic, reorganisation and post-independence events
match: गणतंत्र के रूप में भारत का उदय
units.note: Overlaps Prelims Paper I subject 1's final heading and Mains Paper II Unit IV's reorganisation heading.

units.title: Cultural heritage with special reference to Madhya Pradesh
units.note: The state reference is explicit, so every example should carry an MP illustration wherever one exists.

units.title: World heritage sites and tourism
units.note: Short list, high yield — same material as Prelims Paper I subject 2.

mains/paper-I/part-a/unit-5.focus: The princely states and the tribal heroes — the most MP-specific unit in the paper.

units.title: Princely states to independence
units.note: Know each state's territory, ruler at accession and the instrument of accession.

units.title: Tribal heroes, named individually
units.note: Nine names are printed in the syllabus itself, so each one can be asked directly — learn the revolt, the year and the region for every name.

mains/paper-I/part-b/unit-1.focus: Physical geography and climate of India, including the mechanisms behind monsoon variability.

units.title: Geographical knowledge in ancient India
units.note: A short, often-overlooked line — do not skip it because it appears first.

units.title: Physiographic divisions
units.note: Three divisions are named; keep the hills, plateaus, rivers and lakes listed separately beneath them.

units.title: Soils
units.note: Type, distribution and the crop each soil supports.

units.title: Climate mechanics
units.note: The upper-air circulation part is the technical core; be able to explain the jet stream's role in plain terms.

units.title: Climatic phenomena and change
units.note: One more phenomenon than the Prelims version of this heading — the Indian Ocean Dipole is added here.

mains/paper-I/part-b/unit-2.focus: Agriculture and water — production, irrigation, food security and conservation policy.

units.title: Crops including millets
units.note: The syllabus names श्रीअन्न (millets) explicitly, so give them their own notes.

units.title: Irrigation
units.note: Technique, source and project are three separate lists in one line.

units.title: Food security and the green revolutions
units.note: Keep the second green revolution and sustainable agriculture distinct from the first.

units.title: Water conservation and policy
units.note: River interlinking and the national water policy are policy items and should be answered with the current position, not only the concept.

mains/paper-I/part-b/unit-3.focus: Resources and industry, with energy as a recurring thread.

units.title: Forest resources
units.note: Types and distribution together, as in the Prelims version.

units.title: Minerals and energy resources
units.note: Pair this with the energy-crisis heading directly beneath it.

units.title: Energy crisis and non-conventional sources
units.note: The same heading appears in Prelims Paper I subjects 3 and 4 at a shallower depth.

units.title: Manufacturing industries
units.note: Five industries are named individually; prepare the location factors for each.

units.title: Food processing
units.note: Links to the agro-processing heading in Mains Paper III Part A Unit I.

mains/paper-I/part-b/unit-4.focus: Disasters, pollution, population and the geography-specific technologies.

units.title: Hazards and disasters, named individually
match: भारत में प्राकृतिक खतरे और आपदाएँ-
split: ओलावृष्टि, कोहरा, बादल फटना, तड़ित झंझा
units.note: The syllabus names each hazard, so each can carry its own question — learn the mechanism, the vulnerable region and the mitigation for every one.

units.title: Environmental pollution
units.note: Cause, effect, control and mitigation for each of the three.

units.title: Population pressure and migration
units.note: The angle here is pressure on resources, not population size as such.

units.title: Remote sensing, GIS and GPS
units.note: Know each acronym's full form, a working application and the Indian programme it is used in.

mains/paper-I/part-b/unit-5.focus: The geography of Madhya Pradesh, described region by region. This unit rewards map work more than any other.

units.title: Physiographic divisions of the state
units.note: Seven named divisions — draw them, then label the districts that fall in each.

units.title: Rivers and tributaries
match: प्रमुख नदियाँ और उनकी सहायक नदियाँ
units.note: River, origin, course and the tributaries that join it.

units.title: Climate
units.note: Seasons, temperature and rainfall for the state.

units.title: Soils and soil conservation
units.note: Conservation is examined alongside the soil types.

units.title: Natural vegetation and forest produce
units.note: Forest types, distribution and the major produce.

units.title: Crops, irrigation and projects
match: प्रमुख फसलें, सिंचाई एवं सिंचाई परियोजनाएँ
units.note: Crop-plus-project recall works best on a river map.

units.title: Minerals and energy
units.note: Mineral belts, thermal and hydro stations, and the non-conventional sources.

units.title: Industry, including small and cottage industry
match: प्रमुख उद्योग, लघु एवं कुटीर उद्योग
units.note: The cottage-industry part is not present in the Prelims version of this heading.

units.title: Population and urbanisation
units.note: Compare with the India-level population heading in Unit IV.

mains/paper-II.focus: Governance and sociology. Part A is institutional and Part B is social — the two are examined separately but often answer each other's questions.

mains/paper-II/part-a/unit-1.focus: The Constitution itself, its ideological content, and the federal-judicial structure.

units.title: Making, features, basic structure and amendments
units.note: The basic-structure doctrine needs its landmark judgments along with the concept.

units.title: Ideological elements
units.note: Overlaps Prelims Paper I subject 5; the Mains version expects reasoning, not recall.

units.title: Federalism and judicial review
units.note: Lok Adalat and PIL are named separately — treat them as their own short topics.

mains/paper-II/part-a/unit-2.focus: Constitutional bodies, then the social bases of Indian politics.

units.title: Commissions and policy bodies
split: संघ लोक सेवा आयोग, मध्यप्रदेश लोक सेवा आयोग
units.note: Five bodies in one line — composition, appointment, powers and mandate for each.

units.title: Caste, religion, class, ethnicity, language and gender in politics
units.note: Use contemporary illustrations; this is an analytical question area.

units.title: Parties, voting behaviour, civil society and national security
units.note: Three distinct strands usually combined into one line here.

mains/paper-II/part-a/unit-3.focus: Democratic participation, organised civil society, media, and political thinkers.

units.title: Features of democracy and citizen participation
split: निर्णय प्रक्रिया में नागरिकों की भागीदारी
units.note: Representation and participation are listed as two ideas; keep them apart in answers.

units.title: CBOs, NGOs and self-help groups
units.note: Define each and give one working example, preferably from Madhya Pradesh.

units.title: Role and problems of the media
units.note: The syllabus pairs role with problems, so both halves are examinable.

units.title: Indian political thinkers, named individually
units.note: Nine names are printed here. Deendayal Upadhyaya and Ahilyabai Holkar are the state-linked ones and recur across papers.

mains/paper-II/part-a/unit-4.focus: Madhya Pradesh's formation and institutions, plus the accountability commissions.

units.title: Reorganisation and partition of the state
units.note: The 1956 formation and the 2000 partition are two separate events — date both precisely.

units.title: Governor, Chief Minister and Council of Ministers
units.note: Appointment, powers and status for each office.

units.title: The state legislature
units.note: The Speaker and Opposition roles are named separately from the House's own powers.

units.title: The High Court of Madhya Pradesh
units.note: Composition, jurisdiction and role.

units.title: Accountability commissions
split: अनुसूचित जाति आयोग, अनुसूचित जनजाति आयोग
केन्द्रीय सतर्कता आयोग, मानव अधिकार आयोग, सूचना आयोग
उपभोक्ता फोरम, बाल आयोग, महिला आयोग
units.note: Nine bodies listed in one line — a table of mandate, composition and complaint route is the fastest way through it.

mains/paper-II/part-a/unit-5.focus: How Madhya Pradesh is actually administered, including local government, tribal and Naxalite issues, and women in state politics.

units.title: State administration and the district collector
split: Secretariat, Chief Secretary, Secretary and Commissioner
District Administration in Madhya Pradesh, Role of District Collector
units.note: The collector's role is the standard case-study anchor for this paper.

units.title: Rural and urban local self-government
match: Rural Local Self Government in Madhya Pradesh-
split: Urban Local Self Government- Organization and Power
Finance Bureaucracy in Local Self Government and importance of autonomy
units.note: Finance and autonomy are named explicitly — the fiscal side of local bodies is examinable.

units.title: Tribal, backward and deprived classes; the Naxalite problem
units.note: A sensitive area: answer with policy and constitutional provisions rather than commentary.

units.title: Women in the politics of Madhya Pradesh
units.note: Representation, reservation and notable office-holders.

units.title: Current issues in state politics
units.note: Dynamic by design — maintain a rolling file, and revise it directly before the exam.

mains/paper-II/part-b/unit-1.focus: Basic concepts of sociology, grounded in Indian usage.

units.title: Indian concept of society and kinship terms
units.note: The source uses Indian categories rather than imported ones — define each in Indian terms.

units.title: Community, institution, association, culture, norms and values
units.note: Five foundational terms in one line; the distinctions between them are the examinable part.

units.title: Social harmony, civilisation and culture
units.note: Salient features of Indian culture are attached to this heading.

units.title: Social institutions
units.note: Note that varna, rin, yagya and sanskar are treated as institutions, not merely rituals.

units.title: Rituals, caste, ashram, purushartha and marriage
units.note: The last clause brings religion and sects into the study of marriage.

mains/paper-II/part-b/unit-2.focus: Diversity, its challenges, and the problems of nation building.

units.title: Conceptualising Indian society
units.note: Unity in diversity is the organising idea of this unit.

units.title: Cultural diversity
units.note: Four kinds of diversity are named; give each an Indian illustration.

units.title: Changing face of crime
split: महिलाओं के प्रति अपराध एवं घरेलू हिंसा
units.note: A current-affairs-sensitive heading; keep data and legal provisions together.

units.title: Tradition and modernity
units.note: A debate, not a fact set — prepare a balanced two-sided argument.

units.title: Problems of nation building
units.note: Links directly to nation building in Mains Paper IV Part A Unit II.

mains/paper-II/part-b/unit-3.focus: Rural and urban sociology, including the 73rd Amendment and town planning.

units.title: Approaches to rural society
match: ग्रामीण समाज के अध्ययन के उपागम-
units.note: The rural-urban distinction is the foundation for the rest of the unit.

units.title: Peasant studies and Panchayati Raj
split: 73वें संशोधन से पहले और बाद में पंचायती राज व्यवस्था
units.note: Know what changed with the 73rd Amendment, not just that it happened.

units.title: Rural development issues
split: ग्रामीण समाज में बदलाव के रुझान
units.note: Bonded and migrant labour are named specifically — this is the social-issue core of the unit.

units.title: Urban community and urbanisation
units.note: Characteristics, change, causes and effects — four parts of one line.

units.title: Town planning and urban management
split: नगर नियोजन को प्रभावित करने वाले कारक
भारत में नगरीय प्रबंध की समस्याएँ
units.note: Overlaps the urban administration material in Part A Unit V and the local-government item in Prelims Paper I subject 5.

units.title: Industrialisation and social change
match: भारत में औद्योगीकरण और सामाजिक परिवर्तन-
split: औद्योगिक समाज में वर्ग और वर्ग संघर्ष
units.note: Impact on family, education and stratification is the examinable list.

units.title: Globalisation, indianisation of sociology and privatisation of education
units.note: Three loosely related items grouped in one line; the indianisation of sociology is the most conceptual.

units.title: Social structure and development
units.note: Facilitators and inhibitors are the analytical pairs to prepare.

units.title: Culture and development
units.note: Culture as aid and as impediment is a standard two-part question.

units.title: Population growth and distribution
match: भारत में जनसंख्या वृद्धि और वितरण-
units.note: Growth since 1901 with causes and effects — the 1901 start point is specified in the syllabus.

units.title: Population concepts
units.note: Definitions and how each is measured.

mains/paper-II/part-b/unit-5.focus: Human resource development and welfare, ending with Madhya Pradesh tribes and folk culture.

units.title: National Education Policy 2020
units.note: Five strands of one policy are listed — prepare each separately, as the syllabus does.

units.title: Welfare issues by social group
match: सामाजिक वर्गों और उनके कल्याण कार्यक्रमों
units.note: Keep the scheme and the constitutional or legal basis for each group together.

units.title: Community development and extension education
units.note: The NGO role here is community development, not the wider media-and-civil-society heading in Part A.

units.title: Tribes of Madhya Pradesh
split: धार्मिक विश्वास, परंपराएँ, त्यौहार और उत्सव
units.note: Study with Prelims Paper I subject 10 — the same facts serve both.

units.title: Folk culture of Madhya Pradesh
units.note: One consolidated folk-culture file covers this, Prelims subjects 2 and 10, and Paper IV.
